newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Rabobank sees Dutch closing rate gap with Germany.
newsitem.headline: Rabobank sees Dutch closing rate gap with Germany.

text.p: Rabobank International said on Monday it was a matter of time before the Dutch central bank raised its special advances rate to close the official interest rate gap with Germany.
In its Financial Weekly report, it added that the rise of the German mark against the Dutch guilder in recent months was expected to continue but not accelerate in the short term.

The Dutch bank said although the difference in economic performance between Germany and the Netherlands was striking, the Dutch special advances rate, at 2.90 percent, was still 10 basis points below its German equivalent, the repo rate.
But as the central bank had an exchange rate target, it would raise the special advances rate, which sets the tone for money market rates, only if forced to act by guilder weakness.
"Given the more and more optimistic growth forecasts for the Netherlands, pressure on the guilder will continue with (the mark) flirting with its central parity at 1.12673 guilders," Rabobank said.
The mark was trading at 1.125750 guilders at 1400 GMT, having risen from below 1.1240 since April.
The Dutch central bank has twice raised the special advances rate this year in response to guilder weakness.

"With the economic rationale for a negative interest rate gap between Germany and the Netherlands completely disappeared and with the guilder losing ground, it seems to be a matter of time before the Dutch central bank closes the still existing gap," Raobank said.
Rabobank attributed the guilder weakness to a perception that central parity rates would probably be used as conversion rates at the launch of the euro currency in 1999.
It also cited the expected divergence of inflation levels between the Netherlands and Germany.
